maya (docs): Quick coordination thread: I'm updating the rate/usage docs to include SDK migration examples (Python, JS) and a fresh Go snippet. Also need to clarify header names for multi-tenant customers (we had a confusion about X-Quota-Org vs X-Tenant-Quota). PR: https://rwd/pulls/4988

gunnar (sdk): Re: headers - current platform accepts X-Tenant-Quota on private deployments and X-Quota-Org on Hosted; we should document both and recommend feature-detecting via /quota metadata. I'll add a small table.

maya (docs): Good — let's avoid implying the headers are guaranteed in all deployments. Can we also include an example that shows checking token-based consumption vs request count? Lots of customers still conflate them.

gunnar (sdk): Yep. Proposed Go snippet (short) to check remaining quota via the /quota endpoint and then make a conditional generate call:

```go
package main
import (
  "context"
  "fmt"
  "os"
  rw "github.com/redwoodinc/redwood-go"
)
func main(){
  client := rw.NewClient(os.Getenv("REDWOOD_KEY"))
  q, err := client.Quota.Get(context.Background())
  if err!=nil{panic(err)}
  fmt.Printf("quota_left_tokens=%d, quota_left_requests=%d\n", q.TokensLeft, q.RequestsLeft)
  if q.RequestsLeft>0 {
    resp, _ := client.Generation.Create(context.Background(), rw.GenerationRequest{Model: "rw-medium", Prompt: "status"})
    fmt.Println("ok id=", resp.ID)
  } else {
    fmt.Println("quota exhausted: use burst or upgrade")
  }
}
```

maya (docs): Couple of nitpicks: 1) use the SDK field names as they are in v2 (snake_case vs PascalCase) — capture exact property names to avoid confusion. 2) add a one-line comment showing how to fallback to quota headers if the /quota endpoint is not available.

gunnar (sdk): Will adapt to v2 names. Also note: the Go SDK currently marshals timestamps differently; I'll sanitize the example to keep it minimal.

pedro (product): Can we include a short paragraph about how burst credits are applied when a team is on a multi-tenant plan vs dedicated? Eg: "multi-tenant: burst rations applied per org; dedicated: pool-level burst with tenant tagging". Keep it non-contractual.

anika (analytics): Add also a short troubleshooting note: "If your dashboard shows zero requests but positive token usage, check for background maintenance jobs that emit embeddings; tokens != requests." That reduces a lot of tickets.

maya (docs): Good. CI/links: I'm trying to embed a Grafana permalink for the "consumption by tenant" panel but deploy-bot flagged the link as internal.

deploy-bot: Link-check: https://grafana/internal/consumption?panelId=99111 returned 403. Suggest using a screenshot artifact or publicly accessible mock link for docs.

maya (docs): I'll attach a sanitized screenshot to the PR; include a caption: "internal panel - screenshot for illustrative purposes". Also adding a small callout: "Panel IDs vary by cluster - use permalink when embedding dashboards in private consoles".

gunnar (sdk): One more: update JS snippet to use client.quota.get() promise example and show both token/request checks. I'll push a commit to the PR.

anika (analytics): For the table showing header differences, include a short line: "When migrating from meter v1 to v2, the X-Rate-Limit-Remaining header is deprecated; prefer /quota or X-Quota-Org/Tenant*".

pedro (product): +1 on the messaging. Suggest we add a tiny migration checklist at the top: "1) audit header names used in your infra 2) update SDKs 3) verify dashboards".

maya (docs): Adding checklist now. Quick ask: please react with :white_check_mark: when you've reviewed the final PR. I'll merge after CI passes and screenshot is attached.
